title: Bright Light
subtitle: Normal vision
description: Bright light lets most creatures see normally. Even on a gloomy day, most outdoor environments are in bright light.

bullets.content: Torches, lanterns, fires, and various spells are common sources of bright light.

title: Darkness
subtitle: Creates heavy obscurement
description: Darkness creates a heavily obscured area. Characters face darkness outdoors at night, within an unlit dungeon, or in an area of magical darkness.

bullets.content: A creature in a heavily obscured area is effectively Blinded.

title: Dim Light
subtitle: Creates light obscurement
description: Dim light, also called shadows, creates a lightly obscured area. An area of dim light is usually a boundary between bright light and darkness.

bullets.content: Creatures in a lightly obscured area have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

title: Half Cover
subtitle: +2 to AC & DEX saves
description: A target has half cover if an obstacle blocks at least half of its body, such as a low wall, large furniture, or another creature.

bullets.content: A target with half cover has a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. If a target is behind multiple sources of cover, only the most protective degree of cover applies.

title: Heavily Obscured
subtitle: Effectively Blinded
description: A heavily obscured area—such as darkness, opaque fog, or dense foliage—blocks vision entirely. A creature in such an area effectively suffers from the Blinded condition.

bullets.content: This means attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's own attack rolls have disadvantage.

title: Lightly Obscured
subtitle: Disadvantage on Perception
description: In a lightly obscured area, such as dim light, patchy fog, or moderate foliage, creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

bullets.content: This penalty applies only to checks that rely on sight.

title: Three-Quarters Cover
subtitle: +5 to AC & DEX saves
description: A target has three-quarters cover if about three-quarters of it is covered by an obstacle, like a portcullis or a thick tree trunk.

bullets.content: A target with three-quarters cover has a +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. If a target is behind multiple sources of cover, only the most protective degree of cover applies.

title: Total Cover
subtitle: Cannot be targeted directly
description: A target has total cover if it is completely concealed by an obstacle.

bullets.content: A target with total cover can’t be targeted directly by an attack or a spell, although it can be affected by spells with an area of effect.

title: Blindsight
subtitle: Perceive without sight
description: A creature with blindsight can perceive its surroundings without relying on sight, within a specific radius.

bullets.content: Creatures without eyes, such as oozes, and creatures with echolocation or heightened senses, such as bats and true dragons, have this sense.

title: Darkvision
subtitle: See in darkness
description: Many creatures in fantasy gaming worlds, especially those that dwell underground, have darkvision.

bullets.content: Within a specified range, a creature with darkvision can see in darkness as if the darkness were dim light, so areas of darkness are only lightly obscured as far as that creature is concerned.
However, the creature can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

title: Truesight
subtitle: Perceive things as they are
description: A creature with truesight can, out to a specific range, see in normal and magical darkness, see invisible creatures, and automatically detect visual illusions.

bullets.content: A creature with truesight also has the following benefits:

items: It perceives the original form of a shapechanger or a creature that is transformed by magic.
It can see into the Ethereal Plane.

bullets.content: This is a rare and powerful form of sight.
